soul_reaver.name: Soul Reaver
soul_reaver.lore: Few who have held the Soul Reaver remember doing so willingly. The blade selects its wielders, and the criteria are opaque. What is known: wounds it inflicts do not heal without magic; the blade whispers between kills; and it grows heavier if used against the innocent. Its origin is attributed variously to a dying god, a betrayed archmage, and a particularly vengeful plague.
soul_reaver.design_notes: Signature chain: finesse opener; the blade hesitates on the first cut (0.2x) and only commits once it tastes blood. Lifesteal makes the long ramp viable.

dawnbreaker.name: Dawnbreaker
dawnbreaker.lore: Dawnbreaker is the hammer that ended the First Darkness, when the elder dead walked the surface and the sun was a rumour. The head holds a sliver of preserved dawn, sealed in adamantine by a smith whose name was burned out of every chronicle the priests could find. The flesh of the dead remembers what it was supposed to fear, and obeys. The gold gleam at the hammer's seam never quite goes out, even in a closed sack.
dawnbreaker.design_notes: Holy/radiant archetype: a building dawn, each strike a fuller rising sun against the undead.

venomfang.name: Venomfang
venomfang.lore: A master poisoner's commission from an earlier age. The spikes of Venomfang are hollow, and the venom inside them was blended from the stings and bites of a hundred different creatures, so that no single antidote answers it. The weapon weeps a thin dark ichor when hungry, which is often. The wounds it leaves do not merely bleed. They sour.
venomfang.design_notes: Cursed-blade archetype: the venom needs time to find the wound, slow first taste then devastating last.

excalibur.name: Excalibur
excalibur.lore: The Lady of the Lake gave Arthur this sword after his first blade broke, and Merlin told him the scabbard was worth ten of it, since its wearer could lose no blood. Morgan le Fay stole the scabbard. Tennyson has the blade engraved on one side 'Take me' and on the other 'Cast me away.' After Camlann, Sir Bedivere hid it twice before he could bring himself to throw it back.
excalibur.design_notes: Signature chain: the king's killing blow -- chain-1 already a meaningful cut (1.0x), then a steep climb to a legendary peak of 5.0x at chain-5.

durendal.name: Durendal
durendal.lore: Roland's sword contained within its golden hilt a tooth of Saint Peter, blood of Saint Basil, hair of Saint Denis, and a fragment of the Virgin's raiment. At Roncevaux, rather than let it fall to the Saracens, Roland struck it three times against a stone. The stone split each time. Durendal did not.
durendal.design_notes: Ancient/stately archetype: measured Carolingian steel, each blow as deliberate as the saints sealed in its hilt.

gram.name: Gram
gram.unidentified_name: a shining foreign blade of pale steel
gram.lore: Odin drove Gram into the oak Barnstokk in King Volsung's hall, and only Sigmund could draw it out. Years later the blade shattered, and the smith Regin reforged the pieces for Sigmund's son Sigurd, who tested the edge by splitting the anvil to its base. With Gram he killed the dragon Fafnir from a pit dug under its path. No hide or mail has turned it since.

broken_gram.name: Broken Blade of Gram
broken_gram.unidentified_name: a broken sword hilt with a jagged blade
broken_gram.lore: These are the shards of Sigmund's sword. In his last battle a one-eyed old man in a wide hat stepped into his path and raised a spear, and the blade broke in two against it. Sigmund understood who had come for him. Dying, he told his wife Hjordis to keep the pieces for their unborn son. It is a poor weapon as it lies, but it is waiting to be made whole.

sigurds_shovel.name: Sigurd's Shovel
sigurds_shovel.lore: An ordinary iron shovel, and proof that not every legend needs a magic sword. Regin told Sigurd to dig one pit in the dragon's path and stab upward as Fafnir crawled to the water. An old man with one eye stopped by and advised digging several more, so the blood would have somewhere to drain. Sigurd dug. The shovel still moves earth and stone quite well.

tyrfing.name: Tyrfing
tyrfing.unidentified_name: a sword that vibrates with cold malice
tyrfing.lore: King Svafrlami trapped the dwarves Dvalin and Durin outside their rock and made them forge a sword that would never rust and would bite iron like cloth. They obeyed, then cursed it: Tyrfing would kill a man every time it left the sheath, work three great evils, and be the death of Svafrlami himself. All of it came true. Hervor later took it from her father's barrow, knowing every word.
tyrfing.design_notes: Cursed-blade archetype: the dwarven curse waits patient; the blade hungers and pays out in full.

fragarach.name: Fragarach
fragarach.unidentified_name: a slender blade with a sea-blue shimmer
fragarach.lore: Fragarach means the Answerer. The sea-god Manannan mac Lir owned it and passed it to his foster-son Lugh of the Long Arm. The Irish tales say that no one with its point at his throat could move or tell a lie, that no armour stopped it, and that the wounds it gave did not heal. Lugh carried it when the Tuatha De Danann threw off the Fomorians.
fragarach.design_notes: King's blow archetype: The Answerer needs no warm-up, every stroke is the Wind from the East.

caladbolg.name: Caladbolg
caladbolg.unidentified_name: a massive greatsword of unearthly make
caladbolg.lore: Caladbolg, the hard cleaver, was the two-handed sword of Fergus mac Roich, and it traced an arc like a rainbow when he swung it. In the last battle of the Cattle Raid of Cooley, Fergus had King Conchobar at his mercy. Talked out of the killing, he turned his rage on the landscape instead and sheared the tops off three hills in Meath. The hills are still flat.
caladbolg.design_notes: Brute/crushing archetype: a sweep that takes the tops off hills carries weight from the first arc.

joyeuse.name: Joyeuse
joyeuse.unidentified_name: a radiant blade that shifts colour in lamplight
joyeuse.lore: The Song of Roland says that Charlemagne's sword Joyeuse changed colour thirty times a day and held the point of the Holy Lance sealed in its golden pommel. The French battle cry 'Montjoie!' was said to come from its name. A sword called Joyeuse was carried at the coronations of French kings for centuries and now rests in the Louvre. It dazzles before it cuts.
joyeuse.design_notes: Trickster/nimble archetype: thirty shifting colours dazzle the eye, quick to find the gap and sharp to exploit it.

hrunting.name: Hrunting
hrunting.unidentified_name: an ancient iron-dark blade etched with serpents
hrunting.lore: Unferth lent Hrunting to Beowulf for his descent into the mere. The poem calls it hardened in the blood of battle and says it had never failed any man who grasped it. In the underwater fight with Grendel's mother, it failed once. That was its single exception.
hrunting._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=52, base=13 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(52) x 1.65), min_level=40, quiz_tier=3.
hrunting.design_notes: Ancient/stately archetype: the patient old blade keeps its measured tempo, until the one strike where it does not.

skofnung.name: Skofnung
skofnung.unidentified_name: a cold grey blade with a dim inner glow
skofnung.lore: Skofnung was the sword of the Danish king Hrolf Kraki, and the spirits of his twelve berserker bodyguards were said to be bound in it. The Icelander Skeggi of Midfirth broke into Hrolf's mound and took it. It came with rules: never draw it with a woman present, never let the sun touch the hilt. A wound from it would close only if rubbed with the Skofnung Stone.
skofnung.design_notes: Bestial/feral archetype: twelve berserkers in the steel, each strike a different one finding its rhythm.

gungnir.name: Gungnir
gungnir.unidentified_name: a perfectly balanced spear of dark ash
gungnir.lore: The dwarf sons of Ivaldi forged Gungnir, and Loki brought it to Odin as a peace offering. It never misses its mark, and an oath sworn on its point cannot be broken. Odin hurled it over the host of the Vanir to open the first war in the world. At Ragnarok he will ride at the wolf Fenrir with it levelled, and the wolf will swallow him anyway.
gungnir._curve_note: Promoted to F90s: peak=91, base=37 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(91) x 1.65).
gungnir.design_notes: King's blow archetype: Odin's throw never wavers, the unbreakable oath strikes with sovereign certainty.

gae_bulg.name: Gáe Bulg
gae_bulg.unidentified_name: a barbed spear of sea-monster bone
gae_bulg.lore: The warrior-woman Scathach gave the Gae Bulg to Cu Chulainn alone of her pupils. It was made from the bone of a sea monster and cast from the fork of the foot. It entered as one wound and opened into thirty barbs, and it had to be cut out of the body. Cu Chulainn used it on his foster-brother Ferdiad and on his own son Connla. He wept both times.
gae_bulg.design_notes: Signature chain: the never-miss spear of Cu Chulainn -- chain-1 is already a confirmed kill (1.0x), and every rung climbs cleanly. No weak openers, no dramatic peak; the spear simply lands.

spear_of_longinus.name: Spear of Longinus
spear_of_longinus.unidentified_name: a Roman pilum with a blackened tip
spear_of_longinus.lore: John's Gospel says that a soldier pierced the side of Christ on the cross, and blood and water came out. Later tradition named the soldier Longinus, said that the blood cured his failing eyes, and made him a saint. Emperors and crusaders fought to own his spear; one was dug up at Antioch in 1098 and carried into battle. The dead and the damned flinch from its point.
spear_of_longinus.design_notes: Holy/radiant archetype: the relic warms as it works, radiance gathered with each righteous thrust.

mjolnir.name: Mjolnir
mjolnir.unidentified_name: a short-handled hammer of unsettling weight
mjolnir.lore: The dwarves Brokkr and Eitri forged Mjolnir on a wager with Loki, who turned himself into a fly and bit Brokkr's eyelid at the bellows. That is why the handle came out short. The gods judged it the best of all their treasures anyway, because it guarded Asgard from the giants. Thor needs iron gauntlets to grip it. At Ragnarok it kills the Midgard Serpent, and Thor walks nine steps and falls.
mjolnir._curve_note: Promoted to F90s: peak=92, base=42 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(92) x 1.75).
mjolnir.design_notes: King's blow archetype: every blow of Thor's hammer lands like the first, no warm-up to giant-slaying.

sharur.name: Sharur
sharur.unidentified_name: a golden mace that hums faintly
sharur.lore: Sharur, the Smasher of Thousands, was the mace of the Sumerian warrior-god Ninurta. It could fly, and it could talk. The old poems send it ranging ahead over the mountains to spy out the demon Asag and report back, and at one point it advises its own master to retreat. Ninurta did not listen, and won regardless. A blow from it leaves an enemy reeling and unsure which way is forward.
sharur._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=45, base=10 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(45) x 1.55), min_level=37, quiz_tier=3.
sharur.design_notes: Trickster/nimble archetype: the talking mace reads the field, quick adapt to where the enemy is not looking.

ruyi_jingu_bang.name: Ruyi Jingu Bang
ruyi_jingu_bang.unidentified_name: a massive iron pillar banded with gold
ruyi_jingu_bang.lore: The Compliant Golden-Hooped Rod began as the iron pillar with which Yu the Great measured the depth of the flood waters. It lay in the Dragon King's undersea palace until Sun Wukong, the Monkey King, walked off with it. It weighs thirteen thousand five hundred catties, grows tall enough to prop up heaven, and shrinks to a needle he kept behind his ear. An enemy several paces off is still within its reach.
ruyi_jingu_bang._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=82, base=30 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(82) x 1.7), min_level=70, quiz_tier=5.
ruyi_jingu_bang.design_notes: Signature chain: the As-You-Will Cudgel -- starts modest, then expands to a climactic spike at chain-5 (4.0x). Sun Wukong's staff grows with intent.

gandiva.name: Gandiva
gandiva.unidentified_name: a great bow that hums with stored energy
gandiva.lore: The fire-god Agni asked the sea-god Varuna for Gandiva, and gave it to Arjuna so that he could hold off Indra's rain while the Khandava forest burned. Its twang sounded like thunder. On the field of Kurukshetra, Arjuna saw his own kinsmen in the opposing line and let the bow slip from his hand. Krishna's answer to him fills the eighteen chapters of the Bhagavad Gita. Arjuna picked it up again.
gandiva.design_notes: Brute/crushing archetype: a hundred strings sing at once, no shot is half-drawn on Arjuna's bow.

fail_not.name: Fail-not
fail_not.unidentified_name: a yew bow with a single carved inscription
fail_not.lore: The poet Beroul tells how Tristan, hiding in the forest of Morrois with Queen Iseult, built a bow and set it so cleverly among the branches that any stag brushing past was struck exactly where it touched. He named it Fail-Not, the bow that does not miss. The promise holds while its archer is calm and unhurt. A wounded hand makes it an ordinary bow again.
fail_not._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=57, base=16 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(57) x 1.65), min_level=45, quiz_tier=3.
fail_not.design_notes: Sniper/precise archetype: the bow waits for the dutiful arrow, patience then a single inevitable strike.

kusanagi.name: Kusanagi-no-Tsurugi
kusanagi.unidentified_name: a slim blade with the scent of rain
kusanagi.lore: Found inside the eight-headed serpent Yamata no Orochi. Yamato Takeru used it to cut the grass and redirect the wind when surrounded by enemies who had set fire to the plain around him. The sword has been at the Atsuta Shrine for fourteen centuries. No one has seen it.
kusanagi._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=83, base=32 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(83) x 1.7), min_level=71, quiz_tier=5.
kusanagi.design_notes: Trickster/nimble archetype: cuts the grass to turn the wind, quick reads then a sharp redirected peak.

zulfiqar.name: Zulfiqar
zulfiqar.unidentified_name: a blade forked at the tip like a serpent's tongue
zulfiqar.lore: Zulfiqar came to the Prophet Muhammad among the spoils of the Battle of Badr, and he gave it to his cousin and son-in-law Ali ibn Abi Talib. After Ali's stand at Uhud a saying went round that became famous across the Muslim world: there is no hero like Ali and no sword like Zulfiqar. Artists draw it with a split point, and one thrust of it finds two enemies.
zulfiqar.design_notes: King's blow archetype: two lives with one thrust, every stroke is the champion's declaration.

harpe.name: Harpe
harpe.unidentified_name: a curved blade with a small hooked back-edge
harpe.lore: Hermes lent Perseus this sickle-sword with an edge of adamant, the only blade hard enough for a Gorgon's neck. Perseus walked up to the sleeping Medusa backward, watching her in the polished bronze of his shield, and struck without once looking at her. The old poets say Cronus used a sickle of the same make against his father the Sky. The shape has a history of ending things that were meant to last forever.
harpe.design_notes: Trickster/nimble archetype: Hermes' gift, quick footwork then a single decisive separation.

trident_of_poseidon.name: Trident of Poseidon
trident_of_poseidon.unidentified_name: a three-pronged weapon of sea-dark metal
trident_of_poseidon.lore: The Cyclopes forged the trident for Poseidon in the war against the Titans. He struck the rock of the Acropolis with it to win Athens, and a salt spring rose. Athena offered an olive tree and won, and he flooded the plain in a temper. The Greeks called him Earth-Shaker, because the same three prongs that raise the sea also split the ground. Odysseus spent ten years learning how long he holds a grudge.
trident_of_poseidon._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=85, base=34 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(85) x 1.7), min_level=73, quiz_tier=5.
trident_of_poseidon.design_notes: Brute/crushing archetype: a sea-god's tide, heavy from the first blow and building to drowning weight.

carnwennan.name: Carnwennan
carnwennan.unidentified_name: a small white-handled knife with no visible edge
carnwennan.lore: Carnwennan means Little White Hilt. The Welsh tale of Culhwch and Olwen lists it among the things Arthur would not give away. When the Very Black Witch had beaten four of his men bloody in her cave at the head of the Valley of Grief, Arthur stood in the doorway and threw the knife. It cut her in two like a pair of tubs. Later tellers said it wrapped him in shadow.
carnwennan._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=34, base=8 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(34) x 1.7), min_level=26, quiz_tier=2.
carnwennan.design_notes: Trickster/nimble archetype: shadows part for the killing stroke, the rogue's blade builds then erupts.

mistilteinn.name: Mistilteinn
mistilteinn.unidentified_name: a blade that seems to cut shadows as well as flesh
mistilteinn.lore: Mistilteinn means mistletoe, the one plant Frigg never asked to spare her son Baldur, because it seemed too young and small to matter. A dart of it killed him. The sword of that name lay in the barrow of Thrain, a king turned draugr, who boasted it had killed hundreds. Hromund Gripsson wrestled the dead man, won, and carried the blade out. It finds the one gap in every defence.
mistilteinn._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=91, base=39 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(91) x 1.7), min_level=85, quiz_tier=5.
mistilteinn.design_notes: Cursed-blade archetype: the one thing nobody guarded against, patient until it finds the gap and then ruin.

curtana.name: Curtana
curtana.unidentified_name: a broad two-handed blade with a blunt squared tip
curtana.lore: Curtana, or Cortain, was the sword of Ogier the Dane, and legend made it a sister to Joyeuse and Durendal, forged of the same steel. When Ogier raised it to kill Charlemagne's son in revenge for his own, an angel stayed his arm. English kings have had a blunt-tipped Curtana, the Sword of Mercy, carried before them at their coronations since the thirteenth century. Now and then it lets a beaten enemy live.
curtana.design_notes: King's blow archetype: mercy is the lesser blade, royal weight in every stroke but the peak stays its hand.

parashu.name: Parashu
parashu.unidentified_name: a divine axe of celestial bronze
parashu.lore: Shiva gave this axe to Parashurama, Rama with the Axe, a sage born into the priestly caste who fought like no priest before him. When a king's sons murdered his father, he swore to clear the earth of the warrior caste and did it twenty-one times over, filling five lakes with blood. Afterwards he taught arms to Bhishma, Drona and Karna. Once the axe starts on an army, it does not lose its rhythm.
parashu.design_notes: Brute/crushing archetype: ten thousand years of penance forged into one axe, heavy from the first arc.

labrys.name: Labrys
labrys.lore: The double-headed axe is cut into the pillars of Knossos and painted on its walls, and it turns up in gold in Cretan caves, too thin ever to have chopped anything. It was a holy sign before it was a weapon. Some scholars think the word labyrinth means the House of the Double Axe. That would make the Minotaur's maze a temple, and this the key to it.
labrys._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=24, base=6 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(24) x 1.65), min_level=16, quiz_tier=2.
labrys.design_notes: Ancient/stately archetype: the priestess's bronze, ritual rhythm building toward the killing blow.

chandrahas.name: Chandrahas
chandrahas.unidentified_name: a curved blade cold as moonlight
chandrahas.lore: Ravana, the ten-headed king of Lanka, once tried to lift Mount Kailash with Shiva still sitting on it. Shiva pressed down with one toe and pinned him there, and Ravana sang hymns of praise for a thousand years until the god relented. Shiva's parting gift was this sword, Chandrahas, the Moon's Laughter, with one condition attached: use it unjustly and it goes straight back to its maker. It still keeps that rule.
chandrahas.design_notes: Cursed-blade archetype: Shiva's gift bides its time, the laughing peak comes only when the price is paid.

laevateinn.name: Laevateinn
laevateinn.unidentified_name: a scorched, wand-thin staff carved with runes
laevateinn.lore: A poem in the Edda says that Loki forged Laevateinn with runes beneath the gates of the dead. The giantess Sinmara keeps it in an iron chest with nine locks. It is the only weapon that can kill Vidofnir, the golden cock at the top of the World Tree, and Sinmara will hand it over only in exchange for Vidofnir's tail feather. No one has yet solved that. Whatever it marks for death goes on dying long after the blow.
laevateinn._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=93, base=40 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(93) x 1.7), min_level=87, quiz_tier=5.
laevateinn.design_notes: Cursed-blade archetype: Loki's wand at Hel's gate, slow gathering of doom then a ragnarok-grade peak.

thyrsus.name: Thyrsus of Dionysus
thyrsus.unidentified_name: a giant fennel stalk topped with a pine cone
thyrsus.lore: The thyrsus is a stalk of giant fennel wound with ivy and capped with a pine cone, and the Maenads of Dionysus carried it into the hills. Euripides says they struck rocks with it and water and wine sprang out. In the same play Queen Agave, out of her mind with the god's frenzy, takes her own son Pentheus for a mountain lion. One tap is enough to leave a mind unsure of what it sees.
thyrsus._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=32, base=7 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(32) x 1.5), min_level=24, quiz_tier=2.
thyrsus.design_notes: Wild/chaotic archetype: Maenad rhythm, the staff lurches in bacchic madness then crowns its frenzy.

rod_of_moses.name: Rod of Aaron
rod_of_moses.unidentified_name: a plain shepherd's crook of ancient wood
rod_of_moses.lore: At the burning bush God asked Moses what he held in his hand. It was a shepherd's rod, and it became a serpent on the ground. Before Pharaoh the rod turned to a serpent again and swallowed the serpents of the court magicians. Stretched over Egypt it brought the plagues, and over the sea it parted the waters. Something of the serpent stays in it, and its blow can poison.
rod_of_moses._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=84, base=31 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(84) x 1.65), min_level=72, quiz_tier=5.
rod_of_moses.design_notes: Holy/radiant archetype: shepherd's rod made instrument of God, the radiance builds with each pronouncement.

amenonuhoko.name: Amenonuhoko
amenonuhoko.unidentified_name: a jeweled spear dripping with brine
amenonuhoko.lore: The elder gods gave the Heavenly Jeweled Spear to Izanagi and Izanami and told them to make the drifting world solid. The two stood on the Floating Bridge of Heaven and stirred the sea below. When they lifted the spear, the brine that dripped from its point piled up and became Onogoro, the first island of Japan. Each life it takes sends that first stillness rippling outward through everything nearby.
amenonuhoko.design_notes: Ancient/stately archetype: the spear that stirred the ocean, every thrust a measured drop of the primordial.

sudarshana.name: Sudarshana Chakra
sudarshana.unidentified_name: a spinning disc of burning light
sudarshana.lore: The craftsman of the gods, Vishvakarma, shaved the blazing edge off the sun to make it bearable, and from the shavings he made Vishnu's discus, Sudarshana. Krishna promised to forgive his cousin Shishupala a hundred insults. At the hundred and first he let the discus go. It took the head and flew back to his finger. It always comes back.
sudarshana._curve_note: Promoted to F90s: peak=93, base=39 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(93) x 1.65).
sudarshana.design_notes: King's blow archetype: Vishnu's discus spins from the start, every revolution is a god's strike.

ridill.name: Ridill
ridill.unidentified_name: a short blade from the dwarf-hoard
ridill.lore: When Sigurd had killed the dragon Fafnir, the smith Regin walked up to the body, drew the sword Ridill and cut out the heart, and asked Sigurd to roast it for him. Sigurd burned his thumb on the meat, put it in his mouth, and suddenly understood the birds overhead. They were saying that Regin meant to kill him. Ridill has opened one dragon already and remembers the way in.
ridill._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=55, base=13 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(55) x 1.5), min_level=43, quiz_tier=3.
ridill.design_notes: Sniper/precise archetype: the theoretical blade, patient and undemonstrated until at last it is.

kladenets.name: Samosek
kladenets.unidentified_name: a blade that seems to move before you do
kladenets.lore: The Self-Swinger of Slavic fairy tales fights on its own. It is found in underground kingdoms guarded by Koschei or a serpent. Heroes who find it never quite understand it. The sword fights; they survive. The sword's autonomy is treated not as alarming but as practical.
kladenets._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=58, base=17 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(58) x 1.7), min_level=46, quiz_tier=3.
kladenets.design_notes: Wild/chaotic archetype: the self-swinger has its own ideas, erratic until it finds the killing stroke.
kladenets._note: design_intent: counterAttackChance=0.25 — Slavic legend "the Sword That Fights Itself" should retaliate on incoming melee. No engine consumer as of 2026-09-27; wire it up when the passive-defense hook lands.

shamshir_e_zomorrodnegar.name: Shamshir-e Zomorrodnegar
shamshir_e_zomorrodnegar.unidentified_name: an emerald-studded curved blade engraved with tiny names
shamshir_e_zomorrodnegar.lore: Persian storytellers say this emerald-studded sword hung at the hip of King Solomon, who commanded the djinn. In the romance of Amir Arsalan it is guarded by Fulad-zereh, a horned demon whose mother's spells made him proof against every weapon but this one. To wear it is to be safe from sorcery. A wound from it mends only with a potion that costs the demon his own brains.
shamshir_e_zomorrodnegar.design_notes: Ancient/stately archetype: Solomon's administration in steel, measured and bureaucratic then decisive.

chrysaor.name: Chrysaor
chrysaor.unidentified_name: a golden-bladed sword of divine origin
chrysaor.lore: When Perseus cut off Medusa's head, two children sprang from her neck: the winged horse Pegasus and Chrysaor, whose name means Golden Sword, and who was born with one in his hand. He became the father of three-bodied Geryon. Edmund Spenser gave the name to the sword of his knight of Justice, a blade Jove had used against the Titans, tempered so that nothing could dull or break it.
chrysaor.design_notes: King's blow archetype: the Golden Sword founded a western kingdom, every stroke carries Pegasus-born light.

caliburn.name: Caliburn
caliburn.unidentified_name: a plain but perfectly balanced blade
caliburn.lore: Geoffrey of Monmouth calls Arthur's sword Caliburnus and says it was forged on the Isle of Avalon. Later romances split the story in two: one sword pulled from a stone to prove a boy was king, another handed up from a lake. Some tellers keep the old name for the first. A sword drawn from a stone has to be earned, and this one still grows with every victory its bearer wins.
caliburn._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=37, base=10 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(37) x 1.7), min_level=29, quiz_tier=2.
caliburn.design_notes: King's blow archetype: the stone-drawn blade carries every blow as proof of the king's right.

brisingr.name: Brisingr
brisingr.unidentified_name: a blade that runs warm to the touch
brisingr.lore: Brisingr is an old Norse poets' word for fire. The same root is in the Brisingamen, the glowing necklace that four dwarves forged for the goddess Freyja and that Loki once stole in the shape of a seal. No saga records a smith naming this sword, but he named it well. The steel stays warm in the scabbard on the coldest floor, and what it cuts tends to catch.
brisingr.design_notes: Holy/radiant archetype: the warm blade kindles as it works, a slow fire reaching its proper heat.

fragarach_the_whisperer.name: Whisperer
fragarach_the_whisperer.unidentified_name: a dagger that makes almost no sound
fragarach_the_whisperer.lore: A blade said to have been forged by the same smith who made Fragarach, intended as its companion. Where Fragarach answered questions loudly, this blade worked silently. Assassins across four centuries reported finding it rather than seeking it. It was present at the deaths of seven significant historical figures. Twice it was present at the survival of one.
fragarach_the_whisperer._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=38, base=9 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(38) x 1.55), min_level=30, quiz_tier=2.
fragarach_the_whisperer.design_notes: Cursed-blade archetype: the silent companion bides its time, patient until the moment of betrayal.

naegling.name: Naegling
naegling.unidentified_name: a grey, age-worn weapon with a notch near the grip
naegling.lore: Naegling was the old grey heirloom sword Beowulf carried against the dragon in the fiftieth year of his reign. It snapped on the dragon's skull. The poet explains that Beowulf's hand was too strong, and overtaxed every blade he ever swung. Young Wiglaf, the only man who had not run, stabbed the beast low, and the dying king finished it with his knife. Naegling has unfinished business with dragons.
naegling._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=54, base=13 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(54) x 1.55), min_level=42, quiz_tier=3.
naegling.design_notes: Brute/crushing archetype: Beowulf's grip was always too strong, heavy from the first cut as the steel braces for the end.

punch_in_the_face.name: Punch in the Face
punch_in_the_face.lore: This is Dad’s fist. It is legendary. It has never missed. It has never needed to miss twice. Scientists have attempted to measure the force behind it and their instruments simply stopped working out of respect.

hunt_captains_sword.name: Hunt Captain's Sword
hunt_captains_sword.lore: The Wild Hunt rides the winter sky across all of northern Europe: a host of dead men, black hounds and a captain who is sometimes Odin and sometimes a damned lord. One tale names King Herla, who must ride until the dog on his saddle jumps down, and it never does. This was the captain's sword. It is half in the world and half out, and it carries the cold of the grave.

wendigo_fang.name: Wendigo's Fang
wendigo_fang.lore: The Algonquian peoples of the northern forests tell of the Wendigo, a gaunt spirit of winter and famine with a heart of ice. It grows with every meal, so it can never be full, and the hungrier it gets the more it eats. This fang was torn from such a creature's jaw. It drinks the warmth and the strength out of whatever it bites, and the wound never feels warm again.

echidna_fang.name: Echidna's Fang
echidna_fang.lore: Hesiod calls Echidna half fair-cheeked nymph and half huge speckled serpent, living in a cave deep under the earth. With Typhon she bore Cerberus, the Hydra and the Chimera, and the Greeks called her the mother of all monsters. This is one of her own teeth. Its venom cannot seem to decide which of her children it takes after, and no two wounds from it fester the same way.

vulcans_brand.name: Vulcan's Brand
vulcans_brand.lore: Cacus was a son of Vulcan, a fire-breathing giant who lived in a cave on the Aventine Hill. He stole the cattle of Hercules and dragged them in backward by their tails so the tracks would point the wrong way. Hercules tore the roof off the cave and throttled him in his own smoke. This blade came out of that cave. It was quenched in a god's forge and never fully cooled.

sling_of_david.name: Sling of David
sling_of_david.unidentified_name: a worn leather strap with a pouch
sling_of_david.lore: King Saul offered the shepherd boy his own bronze helmet and coat of mail. David tried them on, could not walk in them, and took them off. He went down to the brook in the Valley of Elah, chose five smooth stones, and met the Philistine giant Goliath with a sling. The first stone sank into the giant's forehead. It is the weapon of the underestimated, and it is never short of stones.

prometheus_torch.name: Narthex of Prometheus
prometheus_torch.lore: Hesiod says Prometheus stole fire in a hollow fennel stalk, a narthex, whose dry pith smoulders slowly inside without burning through. He carried the ember down to mortals that way. Zeus chained him to a crag in the Caucasus and sent an eagle for his liver every day. The stalk still smokes at the core and throws a steady light. It has not gone out in three thousand years.

sword_of_damocles.name: Sword of Damocles
sword_of_damocles.unidentified_name: a jeweled blade with a frayed horsehair knotted at the pommel
sword_of_damocles.lore: Cicero tells the story. Damocles, a flatterer at the court of Dionysius of Syracuse, kept saying how happy a tyrant must be, so Dionysius sat him on a golden couch at a banquet. Then Damocles looked up. A sword hung over his neck by a single horsehair, and he begged to go home. The blade cuts magnificently, but its luck is on a thread, and every miss frays it.
sword_of_damocles.design_notes: Wild/chaotic archetype: each swing thins the horsehair, the blade lurches between safety and the falling sword.

robin_hoods_longbow.name: Robin Hood's Longbow
robin_hoods_longbow.unidentified_name: a weathered yew longbow wrapped in green cloth
robin_hoods_longbow.lore: The old ballads say Robin Hood could split a willow wand at a distance other archers would not attempt, and they put him in Sherwood or in Barnsdale with a yew bow and a coat of Lincoln green. Dying at Kirklees Priory, he shot one last arrow through the window and asked to be buried where it fell. The bow favours an archer nobody has seen yet.
robin_hoods_longbow.design_notes: Sniper/precise archetype: the outlaw's patient breath, the last shot from cover splits the arrow before it.

achilles_spear.name: Achilles's Spear
achilles_spear.unidentified_name: a bronze-tipped ash spear with a worn grip
achilles_spear.lore: The centaur Chiron cut this ash on Mount Pelion and gave it to Peleus on his wedding day. Peleus passed it to his son, and Homer says no other Greek could even lift it. Patroclus took all the rest of Achilles's armour and left the spear behind. Rust scraped from its point healed King Telephus of the wound it had given him, and it still gives back strength as it takes life.
achilles_spear.design_notes: Ancient/stately archetype: Hephaestus' shaft, measured and deliberate; the rust on its tip already knowing the cure.

gilgamesh_axe.name: Gilgamesh's Axe
gilgamesh_axe.unidentified_name: a heavy bronze axe with cuneiform inscriptions
gilgamesh_axe.lore: Before they met, Gilgamesh dreamed that an axe lay in the street of Uruk and that he loved it like a wife. His mother told him the axe was a man, a friend who would never forsake him. That friend was Enkidu. The smiths of Uruk cast great axes for the two of them, and they carried them to the Cedar Forest to face its guardian Humbaba.
gilgamesh_axe.design_notes: Bestial/feral archetype: the axe Enkidu dreamed, primal rhythm; the bond hardens it after the first wound.

cronus_scythe.name: Cronus's Scythe
cronus_scythe.unidentified_name: a curved blade that distorts the air around it
cronus_scythe.lore: Gaia, the Earth, made a great sickle of grey adamant and asked her children who would use it against their father. Only Cronus, the youngest Titan, said yes. He lay in ambush and cut the Sky away from the Earth for good. The Furies and the Giants rose where the blood fell. Cronus was later equated with Time, and what his blade wounds seems to age as it bleeds.
cronus_scythe.design_notes: Cursed-blade archetype: time itself sheds from its edge, slow as it drinks vitality then ruinous at the harvest.

spear_of_lugh.name: Spear of Lugh
spear_of_lugh.lore: One of the four treasures of the Tuatha De Danann, brought from the island city of Gorias. No battle was ever sustained against it or against the man who held it. Later tales say it thirsted so badly for blood that its head had to be kept steeped in a cauldron, or it would burst into flame. Lugh carried it to Mag Tuired, where he put out the killing eye of Balor, and it has hated a baleful stare ever since.
spear_of_lugh.design_notes: Brute/crushing archetype: a spear quenched in poison strikes hot from the cauldron, heavy from the first lunge.

gae_dearg.name: Gae Dearg
gae_dearg.unidentified_name: a crimson-stained spear that weeps red
gae_dearg.lore: Diarmuid Ua Duibhne of the Fianna owned two spears. Gae Buidhe, the Yellow, was for small troubles. Gae Dearg, the Red, was for mortal danger, and no wound it gave ever healed. On the morning he went to hunt the boar of Ben Bulben, Diarmuid took the Yellow Spear against Grainne's advice. The boar killed him. This is the one he should have carried.
gae_dearg.design_notes: Cursed-blade archetype: the Red Spear offers no mercy, patient wound-finding then unhealing ruin.

net_of_hephaestus.name: Net of Hephaestus
net_of_hephaestus.lore: Hephaestus, the lame smith of the gods, learned that his wife Aphrodite was meeting Ares in secret. He forged a net of chains as fine as spider silk, too thin to see and too strong for the god of war to break, and dropped it over them. Then he called all Olympus to look, and the gods laughed for a long time. The net does almost no harm. Nothing gets out of it.
net_of_hephaestus.design_notes: Trickster/nimble archetype: the smith-god's ensnaring weave, light strokes that find the gaps then the closing fold.

sword_of_michael.name: Sword of Michael
sword_of_michael.unidentified_name: a blade of blinding white radiance
sword_of_michael.lore: The sword of the Archangel Michael, captain of the armies of Heaven. The Book of Revelation tells of war in heaven, where Michael and his angels fought the dragon and cast him down to the earth. No armour, enchantment or infernal hide can turn this edge, and against the Destroyer it blazes with the full wrath of Heaven. It is not won by strength. It is given to a soul that has been weighed and found worthy.

oathkeeper_sword.name: Oathkeeper
oathkeeper_sword.unidentified_name: a well-kept longsword with a name on the crossguard
oathkeeper_sword.lore: A longsword of excellent make, with the name VALE engraved on the crossguard. A young man carried it into the dungeon to prove himself, and he did not come back. The blade is still sharp, and someone oiled and honed it with love for years. It strikes best when its bearer has a companion fighting at his side.

penitents_blade.name: Penitent's Blade
penitents_blade.unidentified_name: a dark iron dagger stained with old blood
penitents_blade.lore: A wickedly sharp dagger of dark iron, carried for twenty years by a man who used it to kill and spent the years after trying to atone. The blade drinks from the wounds it makes and returns the strength to the hand that holds it, as though it were trying to balance a ledger. Used long enough against evil things, it may yet come out even.

boomstick.name: Boomstick
boomstick.lore: This is my BOOMSTICK! It's a twelve-gauge double-barreled Remington. S-Mart's top of the line. You can find this in the sporting goods department. That's right, this sweet baby was made in Grand Rapids, Michigan. Retails for about $109.95. It's got a walnut stock, cobalt blue steel, and a hair trigger. That's right. Shop smart. Shop S-Mart.
boomstick.design_notes: Signature chain: explosive peak -- chain-5 triggers an AOE/shotgun spread. Requires combat.py wiring for the AOE. peak_floor=0 so baseDamage is special-cased (not formula-derived).

chainsaw_prosthetic.name: Chainsaw Prosthetic
chainsaw_prosthetic.unidentified_name: a chainsaw bolted to an arm stump
chainsaw_prosthetic.lore: A Homelite XL chainsaw, permanently bolted to the stump of a severed right hand. The original owner attached it in a moment of desperate improvisation in a remote cabin in Tennessee. It has since carved through more deadites than anyone cares to count. Groovy.

romulus_spear.name: Spear of Romulus
romulus_spear.unidentified_name: a bronze-tipped spear with wolf-hide grip
romulus_spear.lore: Plutarch says that Romulus once tested his arm by hurling a spear of cornel wood from the Aventine Hill to the Palatine. The point buried itself so deep that no one could pull it out, and the shaft took root and grew into a tree the Romans fenced and tended for centuries. He was nursed by a she-wolf and killed his own brother over a wall. The spear reaches further than a common one.

pharaohs_crook.name: Pharaoh's Crook
pharaohs_crook.lore: Every pharaoh was shown holding two things crossed on his chest: the crook, called heka, and the flail. The crook is a shepherd's tool, and it meant that the king was herdsman of his people. The same sign was the hieroglyph for the word 'ruler.' This one, striped in gold and blue, once lay in the folded arms of a king. Those who stand beside its bearer stand a little taller.
pharaohs_crook.design_notes: King's blow archetype: every stroke carries pharaoh's authority, even the first touch is rebuke.

mjolnir_shard.name: Mjolnir Shard
mjolnir_shard.unidentified_name: a heavy iron fragment crackling with static
mjolnir_shard.lore: A jagged fragment of iron that claims to be a piece of Mjolnir, the hammer the dwarves Brokkr and Eitri made for Thor. The myths never say the hammer chipped, but lightning arcs across the break all the same and every blow lands with a mutter of distant thunder. Norsemen wore small hammers on a cord for protection. This is a good deal heavier than an amulet.
mjolnir_shard.design_notes: Signature chain: heavy with thunder peak -- a chip of the hammer keeps the weight even when broken. NOTE: chain-5 should trigger a lightning status proc; requires combat.py wiring.

bow_of_rama.name: Bow of Rama
bow_of_rama.unidentified_name: a recurved bow radiating faint heat
bow_of_rama.lore: To win Sita's hand a suitor had to string the great bow of Shiva. Prince Rama lifted it, bent it, and snapped it in two with a crack like thunder. His own bow, Kodanda, went with him through fourteen years of forest exile and across the sea to Lanka, where his arrow brought down the ten-headed demon king Ravana. Its shafts fly hot, and demons have reason to fear them.

gae_bolg_fragment.name: Gae Bolg Fragment
gae_bolg_fragment.unidentified_name: a barbed bone spearhead bound to a shaft
gae_bolg_fragment.lore: A broken length of the Gae Bulg, the spear the warrior-woman Scathach taught only Cu Chulainn to throw. The whole weapon was carved from the bone of a sea beast that died fighting another, and its head opened into barbs once it was inside the body. Even this piece, lashed to a new shaft, will not come out of a wound cleanly.
gae_bolg_fragment.design_notes: Cursed-blade archetype: even the splinter remembers, the bone barbs find the wound and then they spread.

staff_of_moses.name: Staff of Moses
staff_of_moses.unidentified_name: a weathered staff of ancient wood
staff_of_moses.lore: This was a shepherd's staff, cut for walking the hills of Midian behind another man's flock. Then Moses raised it over the Red Sea and the waters stood up like walls. At Horeb he struck the rock with it and water ran for a thirsty people. At Rephidim, Israel prevailed for as long as he held it high. The wood is ordinary. What matters is the hand that holds it and the God who sent him.
staff_of_moses.design_notes: Holy/radiant archetype: the shepherd's rod chosen by God, the radiance grows as the unholy is named.

witcher_silver_blade.name: Witcher's Silver Blade
witcher_silver_blade.unidentified_name: a blade of polished silver etched with runes
witcher_silver_blade.lore: A witcher carries two swords: steel for men, silver for monsters. This is the silver one, made for wraiths, vampires, ghouls and the nameless things that crawl out of cursed earth. A white-haired witcher bore it through a hundred contracts, never quite human and never the monster people took him for. The runes along its edge hum faintly when dark magic is near.

zireael.name: Zireael
zireael.unidentified_name: an impossibly light sword with a swallow engraved on the blade
zireael.lore: Zireael means Swallow in the Elder Speech. The gnome swordsmith Esterhazy of Mahakam made it, lighter than any sword of human forging and harder than dwarven steel, for a girl with the blood of the Elder Folk in her veins. The swallow engraved on the blade is a promise as much as a decoration: she comes back. In the right hand it is so quick that one kill flows straight into the next stroke.
zireael.design_notes: Signature chain: Swallow, the witcher's blade -- fast finesse opener (0.4x) with a sharp closing peak. Rewards the chain.

vel_of_murugan.name: Vel of Murugan
vel_of_murugan.unidentified_name: a bronze lance that radiates heat
vel_of_murugan.lore: Parvati gave the Vel, a leaf-bladed lance, to her son Murugan when he rode out against the demon Surapadman. The demon turned himself into a great mango tree in the sea, and the Vel split him down the middle. One half became a peacock, which Murugan took as his mount. The other became a rooster, which he put on his banner. The lance burns, and no shield turns it.
vel_of_murugan.design_notes: Holy/radiant archetype: Parvati's lance burns with righteous war, a steady building flame: peacock and rooster.

khopesh_of_anubis.name: Khopesh of Anubis
khopesh_of_anubis.unidentified_name: a curved sickle-blade of black iron
khopesh_of_anubis.lore: Anubis weighed the heart of every Egyptian dead against the feather of Ma'at, truth itself. If the heart was heavier, the demon Ammit ate it on the spot. The priests of Anubis carried khopeshes of black iron during the embalming rites, not for use on the living but for the symbolic severing of what could not be allowed into the next world. This is one of them. The blade still measures, and what it judges, it keeps.
khopesh_of_anubis.design_notes: Cursed-blade archetype: the embalmer's reckoning, quiet at first then the heart is found too heavy.

chandrahasa.name: Chandrahasa
chandrahasa.unidentified_name: a crescent-shaped blade that glows faintly
chandrahasa.lore: Chandrahasa, the Laughing Moon, was the sword Shiva gave to Ravana, the demon king of Lanka, with a warning never to draw it unjustly. Ravana drew it when the old vulture-king Jatayu tried to stop him carrying off Sita, and cut the bird's wings from his body. The blade laughs as it cuts, a high cold sound like cracking ice, and it bites deepest when its bearer is nearest to death.
chandrahasa._curve_note: Pass 3 trim: peak=87, base=34 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(87) x 1.65).
chandrahasa.design_notes: Cursed-blade archetype: the Laughing Moon ripens on desperation, patient until the wielder's strength fades.

green_chapel_axe.name: Green Chapel Axe
green_chapel_axe.unidentified_name: a green-hafted axe with living vines
green_chapel_axe.lore: The Green Knight carried this axe into Arthur's hall on New Year's Day and offered a game: any knight might strike him one blow, if he might return it in a year. Gawain took the challenge and cut off his head. The Knight picked it up and rode out. A year later, at the Green Chapel, the return stroke only nicked Gawain's neck. A wound taken while holding the axe begins to close, slowly but surely.
green_chapel_axe.design_notes: Bestial/feral archetype: the Green Knight's pact, strike then take then strike again: primal exchange-rhythm.

aiglos.name: Aiglos
aiglos.unidentified_name: a long white-shafted spear rimed with frost
aiglos.lore: Snow-point, the spear of Gil-galad the last High King of the Noldor, who fell at the Last Alliance before the gates of Barad-dur. He hewed at the Dark Lord himself with this and was burned to ash by the contact. The spear endured. It does not lose its edge and it does not warm in the hand.
aiglos._curve_note: base_damage = curve.weapon_base_damage(86) x 1.7 unique-mult. Class: heavy 5-rung [0.75, 0.90, 1.00, 1.30, 1.75]. F80-89 Fenrir-era band fill; LOTR signature.
aiglos.design_notes: Signature chain: Elendil's spear -- steady, reliable, no surprises. Every rung climbs by ~0.3x; the spear keeps its word.

akinakes_acrisius.name: Akinakes of Acrisius
akinakes_acrisius.unidentified_name: a short leaf-bladed dagger in a gold-faced sheath
akinakes_acrisius.lore: The short, leaf-shaped blade of Acrisius, king of Argos, who locked his daughter Danae in a bronze tower because an oracle said her son would kill him. Perseus killed him anyway, by accident, with a discus throw at funeral games. The blade survived the prophecy. The blades always do.
akinakes_acrisius._curve_note: base_damage = curve.weapon_base_damage(48) x 1.4 unique-mult, finesse precision (8 x 1.4 = 11.2 -> 11). Class: finesse 5-rung [0.20, 0.55, 1.00, 1.80, 3.00]. F40-49 Medusa-era band fill.

anduril.name: Anduril
anduril.unidentified_name: a long bright sword engraved with seven stars
anduril.lore: Flame of the West, reforged from the shards of Narsil by the smiths of Imladris. The blade that cut the Ring from Sauron's hand, broken when Isildur fell, sleeping for an Age in Rivendell until the Heir of Elendil came to claim it. The Dead of Dunharrow followed it down the Paths and a city held the line.
anduril._curve_note: base_damage = curve.weapon_base_damage(84) x 1.6 unique-mult. Class: normal 5-rung [0.50, 0.85, 1.00, 1.45, 2.00]. F80-89 Fenrir-era band fill; signature LOTR Northern-fantasy entry.
anduril.design_notes: Signature chain: the Flame of the West -- a bright, steady ramp. Each rung is meaningful; no dead opener.

atalanta_bow.name: Atalanta's Bow
atalanta_bow.unidentified_name: a light hunting bow with a bearskin grip
atalanta_bow.lore: The huntress raised by bears, fastest of mortals, who drew first blood on the Calydonian Boar before any of the heroes could land a spear. Meleager awarded her the hide, and his uncles died for the slight. Her arrow flies straight to the first thing that draws breath in her sights.
atalanta_bow._curve_note: base_damage = curve.weapon_base_damage(27) x 1.5 unique-mult, rounded. Class: finesse 5-rung [0.20, 0.55, 1.00, 1.80, 3.00]. F20-29 Asterion-era band fill.

bellerophon_lance.name: Bellerophon's Lance
bellerophon_lance.unidentified_name: a long lance with a lump of lead on its point
bellerophon_lance.lore: Tipped with a lump of lead, this is the lance Bellerophon couched from the back of Pegasus when he charged the Chimera. The monster's own fire melted the lead in its throat, and the molten metal did the killing the spearhead alone could not. Pride later threw Bellerophon off the winged horse; the lance survived him.
bellerophon_lance._curve_note: base_damage = curve.weapon_base_damage(42) x 1.6 unique-mult. Class: heavy 5-rung [0.75, 0.90, 1.00, 1.30, 1.75]. F40-49 Medusa-era band fill.

cadmus_sword.name: Sword of Cadmus
cadmus_sword.unidentified_name: a notched bronze sword with a great tooth set in the pommel
cadmus_sword.lore: Cadmus of Tyre slew the great water-dragon of Ares at the spring that would water Thebes. Athena told him to sow the teeth in the furrow; the Sown Men sprang up armed and killed each other until five remained to found the city. The sword that opened the dragon is the same sword that opened the founding line.
cadmus_sword._curve_note: base_damage = curve.weapon_base_damage(44) x 1.5 unique-mult. Class: normal 5-rung [0.50, 0.85, 1.00, 1.45, 2.00]. F40-49 Medusa-era band fill.

glamdring.name: Glamdring
glamdring.unidentified_name: a long pale sword in a jeweled, rune-cut scabbard
glamdring.lore: Foe-Hammer, the orc-cleaver. Forged in Gondolin during the First Age, lost when the hidden city burned, recovered from a stone-troll's hoard in the wilderlands. Gandalf carried it through Moria and into the deep where the Balrog waited. The blade glows blue when goblins are near, which is most of the time, this far down.
glamdring._curve_note: base_damage = curve.weapon_base_damage(82) x 1.8 unique-mult. Class: heavy 5-rung [0.75, 0.90, 1.00, 1.30, 1.75]. F80-89 Fenrir-era band fill.
glamdring.design_notes: Signature chain: the Foe-hammer -- a bright, steady ramp like Anduril. Goblin-bane reliability over flashy peaks.

hector_javelin.name: Hector's Javelin
hector_javelin.unidentified_name: a bronze-headed javelin with a gold ring at the socket
hector_javelin.lore: The bronze-headed javelin of Hector, breaker of horses, last shield of Troy. He threw one like it at Ajax in the duel before the ships; it struck the boss of the shield and bent. Patroclus wore Achilles's armor when he fell to the next throw of its kind.
hector_javelin._curve_note: base_damage = curve.weapon_base_damage(22) x 1.4 unique-mult, rounded for heavy spear feel. Class: heavy 5-rung [0.75, 0.90, 1.00, 1.30, 1.75]. F20-29 Asterion-era band fill.

heracles_club.name: Heracles's Olive-Club
heracles_club.unidentified_name: a knotted olive-wood club dark with resin
heracles_club.lore: Heracles cut this club himself from a wild olive tree near Nemea, on the way to his first labour. The Nemean Lion's hide turned every arrow and blade he tried, so he stunned it with the club and strangled it. He carried the same piece of wood through the eleven labours that followed. It is dark with old work and still smells of resin.
heracles_club._curve_note: base_damage = curve.weapon_base_damage(46) x 2.0 unique-mult, signature boss-tier hero weapon. Class: heavy 5-rung [0.75, 0.90, 1.00, 1.30, 1.75]. F40-49 Medusa-era band fill.
heracles_club.design_notes: Signature chain: the Olive-Club -- first hits crush evenly (1.0x, 1.0x), then break into a huge peak. Heracles never warms up; he finishes.

hofud.name: Hofud
hofud.unidentified_name: a bright sword with a watchful face cast on the pommel
hofud.lore: Hofud, called Man-Head, the sword of Heimdall the watcher at Bifrost. He hears wool growing on the backs of sheep and grass climbing out of the ground. At Ragnarok he and Loki will meet on the field and finish each other; the sword will not survive that day either, but until then nothing slips past it.
hofud._curve_note: base_damage = curve.weapon_base_damage(80) x 1.6 unique-mult. Class: normal 5-rung [0.50, 0.85, 1.00, 1.45, 2.00]. F80-89 Fenrir-era band fill; Norse signature.

meleager_spear.name: Meleager's Boar-Spear
meleager_spear.unidentified_name: a broad-bladed ash spear with a crossbar below the head
meleager_spear.lore: The ash-shafted spear with which Meleager pinned the Calydonian Boar that Artemis sent in vengeance for a forgotten sacrifice. His mother carried a brand from his birth-fire; when he killed her brothers over Atalanta's prize, she threw it on the hearth, and the hero burned with it. The spear was a king's weapon either way.
meleager_spear._curve_note: base_damage = curve.weapon_base_damage(26) x 1.8 unique-mult, rounded. Class: heavy 5-rung [0.75, 0.90, 1.00, 1.30, 1.75]. F20-29 Asterion-era band fill.

pelops_sword.name: Sword of Pelops
pelops_sword.unidentified_name: an old bronze sword with an ivory grip
pelops_sword.lore: Pelops won the kingdom of Pisa in a chariot race against King Oenomaus, after bribing the charioteer Myrtilus to swap the bronze linchpins for wax. The king died in the wreck. Pelops then threw Myrtilus into the sea, and the drowning man cursed his house. The sword passed down to Atreus, then to Agamemnon, and Mycenae did not stop bleeding for three generations.
pelops_sword._curve_note: Redistributed: peak=36, base=9 (= curve.weapon_base_damage(36) x 1.55), min_level=29, quiz_tier=2.

stormbringer.name: Stormbringer
stormbringer.unidentified_name: a huge black sword cut with red runes
stormbringer.lore: Black runesword, forged by the Lords of Chaos at the dawn of the Young Kingdoms. It drinks souls and feeds them to its bearer; Elric of Melnibone leaned on it for his strength and lost everyone he loved to its hunger. At the end of the world the blade laughed and named itself a god. It will turn in the hand if the chance is right.
stormbringer._curve_note: base_damage = curve.weapon_base_damage(88) x 1.8 unique-mult, boss-tier signature. Class: heavy 5-rung [0.75, 0.90, 1.00, 1.30, 1.75]. F80-89 Fenrir-era band fill; Elric / Moorcock canon.
stormbringer.design_notes: Signature: chain-5 drains the victim's soul (lifesteal-style heal). Requires combat.py wiring for the soul-steal proc; chain curve here is the runesword's tempered finesse profile.

talos_sickle.name: Sickle of Talos
talos_sickle.unidentified_name: a curved bronze sickle with a rippled edge
talos_sickle.lore: Talos was the bronze giant who walked the shores of Crete three times a day, with a single vein of ichor sealed at his ankle by a bronze nail. Medea charmed him and drew the nail, and his lifeblood ran out like molten lead into the sand. This curved blade is said to be ground from one of the cooled drops. Whatever it is made of still cuts.
talos_sickle._curve_note: base_damage = curve.weapon_base_damage(25) x 1.5 unique-mult. Class: finesse 5-rung [0.20, 0.55, 1.00, 1.80, 3.00]. F20-29 Asterion-era band fill.

theseus_club.name: Theseus's Club
theseus_club.unidentified_name: a short bronze-bound club worn smooth at the grip
theseus_club.lore: The bronze club Theseus took from the corpse of Periphetes, the lame brigand of Epidaurus who beat travellers to death with it. Theseus kept the weapon for the rest of the road to Athens and carried it down into the labyrinth. The hero who walked the maze did not walk it empty-handed.
theseus_club._curve_note: base_damage = curve.weapon_base_damage(23) x 1.5 unique-mult. Class: normal 5-rung [0.50, 0.85, 1.00, 1.45, 2.00]. F20-29 Asterion-era band fill.

cain_club.name: Cain's Club
cain_club.unidentified_name: a crude root-end cudgel stained at the head
cain_club.lore: Genesis says only that Cain rose up against his brother Abel in the field. It does not name the weapon, and commentators have guessed for centuries: a stone, a staff, a rough club made of nothing in particular. God set a mark on Cain so that no one would kill him, but it did not protect him from memory. The wood is the wrong colour at one end and will not wash clean.
cain_club._curve_note: Pass 4: bumped base damage to 4 to match band effective ratio (~2.0x of curve at low floor scales).

wepwawet_mace.name: Mace of Wepwawet
wepwawet_mace.unidentified_name: a slender ceremonial mace topped with a jackal
wepwawet_mace.lore: Wepwawet, the Opener of the Ways, was a jackal god of Upper Egypt, older than Anubis and at first separate from him. His standard was carried in front of the king's procession and in front of the army, and he is shown with a mace and a bow. The pear-shaped mace was Egypt's first royal weapon: on the Narmer Palette the king raises one over a kneeling enemy. This one opens walls as well.
wepwawet_mace._curve_note: Pass 4: bumped base damage to 4 to match band effective ratio (~2.0x of curve at low floor scales).

cuchulainn_hurley.name: Setanta's Hurley
cuchulainn_hurley.unidentified_name: a worn ash hurling stick with a stone-hard heel
cuchulainn_hurley.lore: Before he was Cu Chulainn he was a boy named Setanta. Arriving late to a feast at the house of the smith Culann, he was attacked by the smith's great guard hound, and drove his hurling ball down its throat with this stick. Then he offered to guard the house himself until a pup could be raised. Culann's Hound, they called him ever after. The heel of the stick is as dense as river stone.
cuchulainn_hurley._curve_note: Pass 4: bumped base damage to 4 to match band effective ratio (~2.0x of curve at low floor scales).

mwindo_axe.name: Mwindo's Conga-Scepter
mwindo_axe.unidentified_name: a small carved axe-scepter inlaid with cowrie shells
mwindo_axe.lore: The Nyanga people of the eastern Congo sing the epic of Mwindo, the little one just born who walked. He came into the world talking, already holding his conga, a fly-whisk scepter. His father tried to kill him and failed. With the conga Mwindo raised the dead, his uncles among them, and he once killed the dragon Kirimu. It is generous to whoever carries it now.
mwindo_axe._curve_note: Pass 4: bumped base damage to 5 to match band effective ratio (~2.0x of curve at low floor scales).
